rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they cannot match the Qur’an after striving, its inimitability is proven and belief obligatory; they should fear the punishment prepared for deniers.
rows.anchor: ظهر أنه معجز والتصديق به واجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The broad verb ‘do’ concisely stands for producing a comparable revelation, an act that encompasses the specific challenge.
rows.anchor: فعبر عن الإتيان المكيف بالفعل الذي يعم الإتيان وغيره إيجازا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stating the necessary consequence in place of the implied result alludes to the proof, magnifies obstinacy, and makes the threat explicit with brevity.
rows.anchor: ونزل لازم الجزاء منزلته على سبيل الكناية تقريرا للمكنى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional uses إن, though the situation calls for اذا, because God does not doubt their inability; the denial interrupts condition and consequence in mockery, addressing their pre-consideration belief that they might succeed.
rows.anchor: فإن القائل سبحانه وتعالى لم يكن شاكا في عجزهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لم governs the jussive because it is restricted to the imperfect and attached to its complement; since it makes the verb past-like, the conditional applies to the combined phrase as ‘if you leave the act.’
rows.anchor: مختصة بالمضارع متصلة بالمعمول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لن negates the future more emphatically than لا.
rows.anchor: كلا في نفي المستقبل غير أنه أبلغ

rows.speaker: سيبويه والخليل
rows.claim: Sibawayh and al-Khalil, in one reported account, treat لن as a primitive particle; in another account from al-Khalil, it derives from لا أن.
rows.anchor: وهو حرف مقتضب عند سيبويه والخليل

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ analyzes لن as لا with its alif replaced by نون.
rows.anchor: وعند الفراء لا فأبدلت ألفها نونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa, وقود means the fuel by which a fire is kindled; with ḍamma it is the verbal noun, though the verbal noun can also take fatḥa.
rows.anchor: والوقود بالفتح ما توقد به النار

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh reports the expression وقدت النار وقودا عاليا; the ḍamma form is a noun, perhaps a verbal noun used as a noun, and is also read here.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه: وسمعنا من يقول وقدت النار وقودا عاليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense is the noun ‘fuel’; if it is instead a verbal noun, an omitted مضاف is understood: ‘its fuel is the burning of people.’
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد به الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حجارة is a plural of حجر, like جمالة from جمل, an uncommon, nonproductive plural pattern.
rows.anchor: وهي جمع حجر. كجمالة جمع جمل وهو قليل غير منقاس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stones are the idols the people carved and worshiped alongside themselves, hoping for their intercession, benefit, and protection from harm.
rows.anchor: والمراد بها الأصنام التي نحتوها وقرنوا بها أنفسهم وعبدوها طمعا في شفاعتها والانتفاع بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He supports identifying the stones as idols with the verse saying that the people and what they worship besides God are hell’s fuel.
rows.anchor: إنكم وما تعبدون من دون الله حصب جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that they are punished by the source of their crime, just as hoarders are punished by what they hoarded; another is that punishment reverses their expectations and heightens regret.
rows.anchor: أو بنقيض ما كانوا يتوقعون زيادة في تحسرهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative identifies the stones as the gold and silver people hoarded and trusted in; al-Bayḍāwī objects that this would not explain why this punishment is specified for disbelievers.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الذهب والفضة التي كانوا يكنزونها ويغترون بها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās says the stones are sulfur; al-Bayḍāwī rejects this as an unsupported restriction that undercuts the verse’s aim of magnifying the fire, while suggesting Ibn ʿAbbās may mean all its stones act like sulfur in ordinary fires.
rows.anchor: فإن صح هذا عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما فلعله عني به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because this Medinan verse followed the Meccan statement that people and stones fuel the Fire, its definite reference is understood as familiar to its audience; the linked sentence presupposes a known story.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت الآية مدنية نزلت بعد ما نزل بمكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire has been prepared and set aside as their punishment.
rows.anchor: هيئت لهم وجعلت عدة لعذابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads أعتدت, from العتاد, meaning equipment or provision.
rows.anchor: «أعتدت» من العتاد بمعنى العدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may be a resumption or a circumstantial clause of النار with an implicit قد; it cannot refer to the pronoun in وقودها if وقود is a verbal noun, because a predicate separates them.
rows.anchor: والجملة استئناف، أو حال بإضمار قد من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge and threat urge strenuous counteraction, yet even against the shortest surah, a numerous, eloquent, fiercely hostile audience did not reply with a countertext and instead left home and risked their lives; this proves prophethood.
rows.anchor: ما فيهما من التحدي والتحريض على الجد وبذل الوسع في المعارضة بالتقريع والتهديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse foretells the unseen: any successful countertext would normally have remained known, especially since critics outnumbered defenders in every age.
rows.anchor: يتضمنان الإخبار عن الغيب على ما هو به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Were the Prophet uncertain, he would not have challenged them so emphatically, lest a counterargument overturn his proof.
rows.anchor: لو شك في أمره لما دعاهم إلى المعارضة بهذه المبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording indicates that the Fire already exists, prepared now for the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: دل على أن النار مخلوقة معدة الآن لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كيف is an interrogative of denial and amazement: denying any state in which their disbelief could occur is stronger than asking ‘Do you disbelieve?’ and fits the following circumstance.
rows.anchor: تعجيب لكفرهم بإنكار الحال التي يقع عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing the disbelievers, the address turns directly to them and rebukes disbelief despite the circumstances that should have led them otherwise: ‘Tell me, in what state do you disbelieve?’
rows.anchor: لما وصفهم بالكفر وسوء المقال وخبث الفعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were lifeless bodies: elements and foods, mixtures and sperm, and embryos formed or not yet formed.
rows.anchor: أي أجساما لا حياة لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave them life by creating and breathing souls into them; فاء marks this as immediately connected with the preceding creation, unlike the later events.
rows.anchor: بخلق الأرواح ونفخها فيكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God causes death when their appointed lifespans end.
rows.anchor: عندما تقضي آجالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next life is resurrection at the trumpet’s blast, or life for questioning in the graves.
rows.anchor: بالنشور يوم ينفخ في الصور أو للسؤال في القبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Return is after resurrection for recompense, or being raised from graves for judgment; disbelief despite this history is astonishing.
rows.anchor: أو تنشرون إليه من قبوركم للحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though they may not yet know resurrection and return, the proofs provided make them effectively informed and remove their excuse; the first creation proves God can revive them again, since beginning creation is no harder than restoring it.
rows.anchor: تمكنهم من العلم بهما لما نصب لهم من الدلائل منزل منزلة علمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the address includes both groups: after proofs of divine unity and prophethood and promises and threats, God recounts general and particular favors, making disbelief especially blameworthy because great favors magnify ingratitude.
rows.anchor: أو الخطاب مع القبيلين فإنه سبحانه وتعالى لما بين دلائل التوحيد والنبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death counts as a favor because it leads to the second, true life, as stated in 29:64; the favor counted is the meaning of the entire story, not each clause separately, since some clauses are past and others future.
rows.anchor: لما كانت وصلة إلى الحياة الثانية التي هي الحياة الحقيقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, believers alone are addressed to remind them of favor and distance them from disbelief: once ignorant, they received knowledge and faith, then die, gain true life, and return to reward beyond human perception.
rows.anchor: وتبعيد الكفر عنهم على معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Life properly means sensory power or what entails it; it is figuratively used for growth, as a precursor, and for human excellences such as reason, knowledge, and faith, as life’s perfection and end. Death is used analogously for each opposite.
rows.anchor: والحياة حقيقة في القوة الحساسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited verses use life and death across bodily, earthly, and spiritual senses: God gives life and death, revives the earth, and revives one who was dead by giving him light.
rows.anchor: قل الله يحييكم ثم يميتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When life is predicated of God, it means that He can be characterized by the knowledge and power associated with life in creatures, or a real attribute of His essence that entails these qualities metaphorically.
rows.anchor: وإذا وصف به الباري تعالى أريد بها صحة اتصافه بالعلم والقدرة اللازمة لهذه القوة فينا

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb reads ترجعون with fatḥa on the tāʾ throughout the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب ترجعون بفتح التاء في جميع القرآن

words: هُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ لَكُم مَّا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a further favor following the gift of life: God created what sustains people and completes their livelihood.
rows.anchor: بيان نعمة أخرى مرتبة على الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For your sake means worldly benefit to bodies, directly or through means, and religious benefit through reflection and recognition of afterlife joys and pains; this is not a purpose that perfects God, but an outcome of His act.
rows.anchor: في مصالح أبدانكم بوسط أو بغير وسط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording indicates that useful things are permitted, without implying that every thing belongs to every individual; the common grant can be apportioned for incidental reasons.
rows.anchor: وهو يقتضي إباحة الأشياء النافعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما encompasses everything on earth only if الأرض means the lower realm, just as السماء can mean the upper realm.
rows.anchor: إلا إذا أريد بها جهة السفل كما يراد بالسماء جهة العلو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جميعا is a circumstantial accusative qualifying the second relative pronoun.
rows.anchor: وجميعا: حال من الموصول الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers ‘turned toward the heaven by His will,’ comparing it to an arrow aimed straight; this fits the word’s root, its preposition, and the following creation. He rejects bodily ‘became even’ as a property of bodies; ‘mastered’ is another reported sense.
rows.anchor: من قولهم استوى إليه كالسهم المرسل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative gloss takes استوى as ‘mastered and ruled,’ supported by the poetic line about Bishr ruling Iraq without sword or bloodshed.
rows.anchor: وقيل استوى أي: استولى وملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heaven means either the celestial bodies or the upper regions.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالسماء هذه الأجرام العلوية، أو جهات العلو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ثم may mark the difference and superiority of the heavens over the earth, rather than temporal sequence, which would conflict with the apparent meaning of 79:30; an alternative reading there supplies a later act of spreading the earth, but is less apparent.
rows.anchor: لعله لتفاوت ما بين الخلقين وفضل خلق السماء على خلق الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God formed the heavens evenly, protected from crookedness and fissures.
rows.anchor: عدلهن وخلقهن مصونة من العوج والفطور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun هن refers to heaven as celestial bodies, which is plural, or to heaven as a plural notion; otherwise it is an ambiguous pronoun explained by what follows.
rows.anchor: ضمير السماء إن فسرت بالأجرام لأنه جمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سبع سموات is either an appositive or an explanatory gloss.
rows.anchor: سموات } بدل أو تفسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The astronomers’ nine spheres are uncertain; even if established, the verse does not exclude additional spheres, and including the Throne and Footstool removes the disagreement.
rows.anchor: فيما ذكروه شكوك، وإن صح فليس في الآية نفي الزائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s complete knowledge explains the excellent, beneficial order of creation and is demonstrated by its precise, wise, merciful design.
rows.anchor: ولكونه عالما بكنه الأشياء كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This knowledge removes doubt about gathering bodily parts after they have dispersed and mixed with similar matter; 36:79 likewise invokes God’s knowledge of every creation.
rows.anchor: وإزاحة لما يختلج في صدورهم من أن الأبدان بعدما تبددت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resurrection proof has three premises: body matter can be assembled and revived, shown by its recurring separation, joining, death, and life in 2:28; God knows its parts and locations; and He can assemble and revive them, as shown by His ability to originate them and create greater things.
rows.anchor: أما الأولى فهي: أن مواد الأبدان قابلة للجمع والحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The flawless, beneficial order of creation demonstrates the knowledge and complete wisdom needed for the other premises of resurrection.
rows.anchor: وأنه تعالى خلق ما خلق خلقا مستويا محكما من غير تفاوت واختلال مراع فيه مصالحهم وسد حاجاتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, and al-Kisāʾī pronounce the هاء in forms such as فهو and وهو with sukūn, by analogy with عضد.
rows.anchor: وقد سكن نافع وأبو عمرو والكسائي: الهاء من نحو فهو وهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The announcement of Adam’s creation and honor, including God’s command that the angels prostrate, is a third favor extending to all his descendants.
rows.anchor: تعداد لنعمة ثالثة تعم الناس كلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذ marks a past time in which another event occurred, while إذا marks a future time; both are annexed to clauses, built like relative forms, used causally or conditionally, and always adverbial because they are nondeclinable.
rows.anchor: وإذا: ظرف وضع لزمان نسبة ماضية وقع فيه أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 46:21, ‘remember the brother of ʿĀd when he warned his people’ means remember the event at that time: the event is omitted and its ظرف stands in its place.
rows.anchor: فعلى تأويل: اذكر الحادث إذا كان كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The عامل for إذ may be قالوا, اذكر understood as in its many explicit Qur’anic uses, or an implicit phrase from the preceding verse; on the last analysis this clause coordinates with خلق لكم within its relative clause.
rows.anchor: أو أذكر على التأويل المذكور لأنه جاء معمولا له صريحا في القرآن كثيرا

rows.speaker: معمر
rows.claim: Maʿmar regards إذ as extra.
rows.anchor: في حكم الصلة. وعن معمر أنه مزيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الملائكة is the plural of ملأك in its original form, like الشمائل from شمأل; مألك is inverted from مألكة, a message, since angels convey God’s messages to people or are messengers to them.
rows.anchor: والملائكة جمع ملأك على الأصل كالشمائل جمع شمأل

rows.speaker: أكثر المسلمين
rows.claim: Most Muslims hold that angels are subtle bodies able to assume different forms, reasoning that messengers saw them in such forms.
rows.anchor: فذهب أكثر المسلمين إلى أنها أجسام لطيفة قادرة على التشكل بأشكال مختلفة

rows.speaker: طائفة من النصارى
rows.claim: A group of Christians holds that angels are virtuous human souls separated from their bodies.
rows.anchor: وقالت طائفة من النصارى: هي النفوس الفاضلة البشرية المفارقة للأبدان

rows.speaker: الحكماء
rows.claim: The philosophers describe angels as immaterial substances distinct from rational souls; one class is absorbed in knowing God and free of other occupation, the exalted, close angels, who glorify without tiring.
rows.anchor: وزعم الحكماء أنهم جواهر مجردة مخالفة للنفوس الناطقة في الحقيقة

rows.speaker: الحكماء
rows.claim: In the philosophers’ account, the second class manages affairs from heaven to earth as divinely decreed; they include celestial and earthly angels.
rows.anchor: وقسم يدبر الأمر من السماء إلى الأرض على ما سبق به القضاء وجرى به القلم الإلهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unqualified address includes all angels; alternatives limit it to angels of earth or to Iblis and his angelic company, who were sent to defeat corrupting jinn that had first inhabited earth.
rows.anchor: والمقول لهم: الملائكة كلهم لعموم اللفظ وعدم المخصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جاعل from جعل takes two objects, here في الأرض and خليفة, because it is future and depends on a subject; it can also mean ‘creator.’
rows.anchor: وجاعل: من جعل الذي له مفعولان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خليفة is one who succeeds or represents another, with its feminine ending marking intensification.
rows.anchor: والخليفة من يخلف غيره وينوب منابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The primary referent is Adam, and more generally every prophet God appoints to cultivate the earth, govern people, perfect their souls, and execute His command; this appointment answers human inability to receive divine command without an intermediary, not any need in God for a deputy.
rows.anchor: والمراد به آدم عليه الصلاة والسلام لأنه كان خليفة الله في أرضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not appoint an angel as prophet because people cannot receive His effusion and command directly; perfected prophets receive angels, while the highest may speak to God without an intermediary, as Moses and Muhammad did.
rows.anchor: ولذلك لم يستنبىء ملكا كما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations take خليفة as a successor to earth’s previous inhabitants, or as Adam together with his descendants succeeding predecessors or one another; the singular may stand for his descendants, ‘one who succeeds you,’ or a collective succession.
rows.anchor: أو خليفة من سكن الأرض قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s announcement teaches consultation, honors the future inhabitant by naming him before creation, and displays his preponderant virtue through the angels’ question and answer; wisdom requires abundant good even when accompanied by lesser evil.
rows.anchor: وفائدة قوله تعالى هذا للملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels express surprise that a corruptor be appointed to cultivate and repair the earth, or that sinful people replace its obedient inhabitants; they seek the hidden wisdom like learners seeking clarification, not objecting to God.
rows.anchor: تعجب من أن يستخلف لعمارة الأرض وإصلاحها من يفسد فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their question is neither objection nor backbiting against humanity: angels are too honored for that, as 21:26–27 says they do not precede God in speech and obey Him.
rows.anchor: وليس باعتراض على الله تعالى جلت قدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels may have known of future corruption from God’s report, the Preserved Tablet, reasoned that infallibility belongs to angels, or inferred it by analogy between the two kinds of beings.
rows.anchor: وإنما عرفوا ذلك بإخبار من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The related verbs all mean pouring: سفك is used of blood and tears, سبك of molten jewels, سفح for pouring from above, and شن (also سن) for pouring from a waterskin’s mouth.
rows.anchor: والسفك والسبك والسفح والشن أنواع من الصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed reading makes يسفك passive; the omitted agent referring to من, whether relative or adjective, is understood as ‘blood is shed among them.’
rows.anchor: وقرىء { يسفك } على البناء للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This circumstantial clause explains the question as a friend asking why a trusted stranger is favored: why appoint sinners when we are sinless and more entitled? Its purpose is to ask what favors humans, not to boast.
rows.anchor: حال مقررة لجهة الإشكال كقولك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels understood humans to combine appetite and anger, which could cause corruption and bloodshed, with intellect, which prompts knowledge and obedience. Considering the powers separately, they thought angels could realize intellect’s benefits without those harms.
rows.anchor: وكأنهم علموا أن المجعول خليفة ذو ثلاث قوى عليها مدار أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They overlooked that appetite and anger, disciplined by reason, yield chastity, courage, resisting desire, and justice; the human composite also enables grasping particulars, inventing crafts, and bringing nature’s potential benefits into actuality, the purpose of succession.
rows.anchor: وغفلوا عن فضيلة كل واحدة من القوتين إذا صارت مهذبة مطواعة للعقل

words: قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s reply asserts knowledge of the wisdom the angels had not grasped, including the good achieved through the human composite and its disciplined powers.
rows.anchor: قال إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both tasbīḥ and taqdīs declare God far removed from imperfection; the terms evoke traveling far through land or water. Taqdīs also means purification, since cleansing removes impurity.
rows.anchor: والتسبيح تبعيد الله تعالى عن السوء وكذلك التقديس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بحمدك is circumstantial: ‘while praising You for teaching us to know You and enabling our glorification’; this qualification prevents the angels’ self-attribution of praise from implying conceit.
rows.anchor: في موضع الحال، أي: متلبسين بحمدك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: We purify our souls from sins for Your sake; the angels set glorification against the corruption (understood by some as idolatry) and purification against the grave vice of bloodshed.
rows.anchor: ونقدس لك نطهر نفوسنا عن الذنوب لأجلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some hold that the lām in لك is extra.
rows.anchor: عن الآثام وقيل: نقدسك واللام مزيدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لَكَ can mean ‘because of what you say’ or simply ‘believe/affirm you.’
rows.anchor: أي لأجل قولك، أو لن نقر لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جهرة originally means reciting aloud and is borrowed for seeing face to face; it is accusative as a verbal noun for a kind of seeing or as a circumstance of the subject or object.
rows.anchor: عيانا وهي في الأصل مصدر قولك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant with fatḥa, جهرة, is either a verbal noun like غلبة or a plural like كتبة meaning ‘those who disclose’; in the latter analysis it must be a circumstantial accusative of the subject.
rows.anchor: وقرىء جهرة بالفتح على أنها مصدر كالغلبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questioners were the seventy men Moses selected for the appointment; another report says ten thousand of his people.
rows.anchor: وقيل عشرة آلاف من قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their requested belief concerned either God, who gave Moses the Torah and spoke to him, or Moses’s claim to prophethood.
rows.anchor: والمؤمن به: إن الله الذي أعطاك التوراة وكلمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The affliction followed obstinate insistence on an impossible demand based on imagining God as a body in a direction and place; such bodily sight is impossible. Sight without modality is possible for believers in the afterlife and for some prophets at times in this life.
rows.anchor: فإنهم ظنوا أنه تعالى يشبه الأجسام فطلبوا رؤيته رؤية الأجسام في الجهات والأحياز المقابلة للرائي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account says a fire came down from heaven and burned them.
rows.anchor: قيل جاءت نار من السماء فأحرقتهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account identifies the صاعقة as a cry.
rows.anchor: وقيل صيحة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further account says troops were heard hissing, whereupon the people fell dead or senseless for a day and night.
rows.anchor: وقيل جنود سمعوا بحسيسها فخروا صعقين ميتين يوما وليلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They witnessed either the affliction itself or its effects.
rows.anchor: ما أصابكم بنفسه أو أثره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They preferred worldly life to the afterlife.
rows.anchor: آثروا الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment is not reduced: the jizya is rescinded in this life, and they are punished in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: بنقض الجزية في الدنيا، والتعذيب في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one will repel either punishment from them.
rows.anchor: بدفعهما عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed after polytheists or Jews said Muhammad orders his companions to do something, then forbids it and orders its opposite.
rows.anchor: نزلت لما قال المشركون أو اليهود: ألا ترون إلى محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In language, abrogation is removing a form from one thing and establishing it elsewhere, as a shadow replaces the sun or as copying transfers text; usage then covers either removal, as wind erasing traces, or copying a book.
rows.anchor: والنسخ في اللغة: إزالة الصورة عن الشيء وإثباتها في غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abrogating a verse means ending the ritual obligation of its recitation, its ruling, or both.
rows.anchor: ونسخ الآية بيان انتهاء التعبد بقراءتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Causing a verse to be forgotten means removing it from people’s memories.
rows.anchor: أو بهما جميعا. وإنساؤها إذهابها عن القلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما is a conditional particle that makes ننسخ jussive and is itself its object.
rows.anchor: وما شرطية جازمة لننسخ منتصبة به على المفعولية

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads ما ننسخ from أنسخ: ‘We command you or Gabriel to abrogate it,’ or ‘We find it abrogated.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر ما ننسخ من أنسخ

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read ننسأها, meaning ‘We defer it,’ from النسء.
rows.anchor: وابن كثير وأبو عمرو «ننسأها» أي نؤخرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings mean ‘We cause someone to forget it,’ ‘We cause you to forget it,’ passive ‘you are made to forget it,’ or ‘We cause you to forget it’ with two implied objects.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «ننسها» أي ننس أحدا إياها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A replacement is better for servants in benefit or reward, or equal in reward.
rows.anchor: أي بما هو خير للعباد في النفع والثواب

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads the hamza as an alif.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو بقلب الهمزة ألفا

words: أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ قَدِيرٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s power encompasses abrogating a verse and bringing a replacement equal to or better than the abrogated one.
rows.anchor: فيقدر على النسخ والإتيان بمثل المنسوخ

words: مَا نَنسَخْ مِنْ ءَايَةٍ أَوْ نُنسِهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes the permissibility of abrogation and delaying revelation: rulings and verses serve people’s welfare and moral completion, which vary with times and persons, as livelihoods do.
rows.anchor: والآية دلت على جواز النسخ وتأخير الإنزال إذ الأصل اختصاص أن وما يتضمنها بالأمور المحتملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some use the verse to prohibit abrogation without a substitute, with a heavier substitute, or of the Qur’an by Sunna, since Sunna is not the replacement; al-Bayḍāwī calls all these arguments weak.
rows.anchor: واحتج بها من منع النسخ بلا بدل، أو ببدل أثقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A missing ruling or a heavier one can be more beneficial; an abrogation can be known by something other than scripture, and Sunna too is brought by God. ‘Better or equal’ concerns benefit or reward, not wording.
rows.anchor: إذ قد يكون عدم الحكم، أو الأثقل أصلح

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites argue that the Qur’an is originated because change and variation are among its properties.
rows.anchor: والمعتزلة على حدوث القرآن فإن التغير والتفاوت من لوازمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī answers that change and variation affect things related to the eternal divine essence’s meaning, not that essential meaning itself.
rows.anchor: وأجيب: بأنهما من عوارض الأمور المتعلقة بالمعنى القائم بالذات القديم
